text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Retailer Vendex International to sell 36 pct stake in rival Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer. (p1)
- Publisher VNU beats Reed Elsevier to 14.9 pct stake in Britain's trade fair and exhibition organiser, Blenheim Group. (p1)
- The Netherlands trails field in Europe in management of listed companies and influence of shareholders - survey.(p1)
- De Telegraaf newspaper trying to sell five pct interest in sports-only commercial TV channel. (p1)
- Parliamentary economic affairs committee disregards invitation by Fokker receivers. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank chairman Peter-Jan Kalff rejects economic ministry proposals for government control of bank mergers. (p3)
- Charter airline Martinair's plans to fly to China from October frustrated by bureaucratic problems. (p3)
- Builder NBM-Amstelland forecasts earnings per share to rise 15 pct this year and 10-15 pct pct thereafter. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Financial Times owner Pearson seeks to buy Het Financieele Dagblad. (p1)
- Dutchman sentenced to five years by Hague court for sex with children in the Philippines. (p1)
- Rabobank earns most from takeover of DAF Trucks by U.S. Paccar. (p2)
- Economic affairs ministry proposes to Samsung that Fokker make wings instead of complete airplanes. (p7)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Inland Revenue alarmed by massive tax-evasion via the Internet. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers demands job guarantee from Samsung. (p3)
- PTT Telecom talks with offshore rivals about worldwide cooperation in chip cards. (p27)
- Rabobank clients can pay via the Internet with smart card from April 1997. (p27)
TROUW
- Royal Dutch Airlines and U.S. partner Northwest Airlines extend cooperation despite quarrels. (p6)
- Printer Enschede/SDU to cooperate with German printer Gieseck & Devrient in producing chipcard. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch car sales in first nine months of 1996 up six percent. (p11)
